meta: Piracetam 800 mg + Ginkgo biloba extract 120 mg + Vinpocetine 5 mg (as listed)
Piracetam: Nootropic (cyclic GABA derivative); Ginkgo biloba extract: Herbal cerebral vasoactive agent; Vinpocetine: Cerebral vasodilator (vinca alkaloid derivative)
Piracetam: N06BX03; Ginkgo biloba extract: N06DX02; Vinpocetine: N06BX18

prescription only; Ginkgo biloba extract: Herbal ingredient in an allopathic combination – prescription use; Vinpocetine: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder, freely soluble in water; melting point 152 °C.

Piracetam: The first 'nootropic'; Giurgea coined the term in 1972. Approved in many European and Asian countries but not in the USA. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1964 by Corneliu E. Giurgea at UCB; marketed 1971. Ginkgo biloba extract: Used in traditional Chinese medicine since at least the 11th century; first encountered by Westerners in 1690 in Japanese temple gardens. A 2026 Cochrane review found small-to-moderate, low-certainty improvements in dementia symptoms. First approval/introduction: Standardised extract approved in Germany (EU) for dementia symptoms. Vinpocetine: A synthetic derivative of the vinca alkaloid vincamine, used in Europe and Asia for cerebrovascular disorders for over 30 years; not an approved drug in the USA. First approval/introduction: Introduced in Hungary 1978 (Gedeon Richter).
Piracetam 800 mg + Ginkgo biloba extract 120 mg + Vinpocetine 5 mg (as listed)

Piracetam improves neuronal membrane function and microcirculation; Ginkgo biloba is an antioxidant and PAF antagonist; vinpocetine increases cerebral blood flow. Combination intended for vascular cognitive impairment, though evidence for fixed combinations is limited.

Piracetam Enhances neuronal membrane fluidity and cholinergic/glutamatergic neurotransmission; improves cerebral microcirculation by reducing platelet aggregation and red-cell rigidity. Used for cortical myoclonus and cognitive impairment. Receptor / target profile: Mechanism not fully defined: increases membrane fluidity, modulates AMPA and cholinergic transmission, reduces erythrocyte adhesion and platelet aggregation.

Ginkgo biloba extract Flavonoid glycosides and terpene lactones (ginkgolides, bilobalide) act as antioxidants, inhibit platelet-activating factor and improve microcirculation and neuronal energy metabolism.
Receptor / target profile: Ginkgolides antagonise platelet-activating factor; flavonoids are free-radical scavengers; improves microcirculation and neuronal energy metabolism.

Vinpocetine Inhibits phosphodiesterase-1 and voltage-gated sodium channels; improves cerebral blood flow and glucose/oxygen utilisation, reduces blood viscosity. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits PDE-1, voltage-gated sodium channels and IKK; reduces calcium influx and has antioxidant activity.
Summary: Rapid, complete absorption; Tmax ~1 h. Not protein bound; not metabolised. Half-life ~5 h. Excreted unchanged in urine – adjust in renal impairment.
Ginkgolide A ~4.5 h; ginkgolide B ~10.6 h; bilobalide ~3.2 h
Summary: Ginkgolides and bilobalide have half-lives of ~4–10 h; renally excreted largely unchanged.
Summary: Rapid distribution; half-life ~4.7 h; metabolised to apovincaminic acid.

Ginkgo biloba extract: With or without food.
Piracetam: Renal function; bleeding in at-risk patients.
Vinpocetine: Blood pressure; ECG in long QT.

Piracetam: Low toxicity; bloody diarrhoea and abdominal pain reported with very large doses. Supportive care; haemodialysis removes it. Ginkgo biloba extract: Limited data; supportive care. Vinpocetine: Hypotension, tachycardia; supportive care.
No randomised trials of this fixed combination identified.
GEM study (DeKosky et al., JAMA 2008) – Ginkgo biloba did not prevent dementia.
Cochrane review of vinpocetine (2003) – insufficient evidence for dementia.
Do not stop suddenly if used for myoclonus
Inform doctor if on blood thinners
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
